correctness.rationale: Both maps preserve the unit cube. Exact comparison with the critical symmetric Perron matrix and strict two-step mass descent proves global extinction, including the spectral equality. Quadratic finite-product expansion, strict transverse contraction, and scalar inverse-amplitude summation prove all limits and the positive coefficient gap. All hypotheses and δ=1 exception are explicit. The standalone verification program ran successfully for asymmetric initial states on K2, C3 and P3.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Arenas et al. compute the WIR second derivative, so the Hessian alone is not original. Their Theorem A does not contain an equality-case global asymptotic amplitude or any comparison with WOR. The continuous-time NIMFA flow has a different nonlinear update map and does not imply the discrete WIR/WOR amplitude coefficients. The 2019 discrete SIS article is materially plausible but inaccessible in full; its coverage cannot be excluded from the abstract alone. A stronger general discrete parabolic stability theorem may offer an abstract route, but was not found to state this concrete exact two-protocol comparison.

value.rationale: WIR and WOR are naturally compared network epidemic protocols whose shared spectral threshold was already highlighted in a 2024 review, and WIR threshold curvature was already calculated in 2023. The new theorem gives a graph-explicit, universally positive difference of first-order critical-time decay coefficients, even though linear thresholds agree, and the exact two-vertex singular recovery endpoint. The quantified temporal prediction informs mathematically meaningful critical finite-horizon modeling rather than a parameter renaming or arbitrary isolated computation.
